newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile shares end lower on sub-par earnings reports.
newsitem.headline: Chile shares end lower on sub-par earnings reports.

text.p: Chile blue chips closed softer with investors analyzing nine-month earnings report which have been weaker than expected, said dealers.
The bolsa is seen opening with a negative tilt with stocks seen generally rangebound as the result of high local interest rates, they said.
"The bolsa will be flat with the IPSA index moving between 95 and 102 points until rates come down," said one dealer.
Central bank officials have said the bank will not ease its restrictive monetary policy until the first half of next year.

The IPSA index ended unofficially down 0.64 percent at 97.99 points. The general IGPA index shed 0.34 percent to 5,368.2 points. Turnover sank to 6.7 billion pesos from 11 billion pesos Thursday, the last trading day before the All Saints public holiday Friday.
Traders noted thin demand for Chilean-issued American Depositary Receipts with a pre-presidential election lull quelling demand for stocks on Wall Street, said dealers.
Electricity stocks are expected to continue to be hurt by the government's review, which has slashed generating rates and is expected to cut distribution rates by a similar amount.
Delays in publishing distribution rates as the result of a legal dispute between power firms and the government are seen adding to the jitters in the sector, said dealers.
"As long as there is no transparency in the rates, there will continue to be uncertainty," said one trader.
Generating company earnings are expected to be hit as growth in demand will not be enough to make up for the 11 percent cut in rates announced by the government last week, said dealers.
Generator Chilgener shed 1.07 percent to 2,320 pesos with Endesa off 0.59 percent at 254-1/2 pesos.
Winners included pension fund manager Provida, up 1.32 percent at 9,575 pesos, winery Concha y Toro, up 0.62 percent at 163 pesos, and bottler Andina, which climbed 0.43 percent to 2,320 pesos.
